meta.title: Tools, Giving & Receiving, and 'Already' vs. 'Not Yet'
meta.objective: Master using the particle で to indicate tools, instruments, and language means; asking translations with 『～語で何ですか』; understanding the directional verbs of giving and receiving (にあげます, に/からもらいます, にかします, に/からかります, におしえます, に/からならいます); mastering Takashi Sensei's critical rule that あげます cannot be used when the receiver is 'me'; answering already (もう～ました) vs. not yet (いいえ、まだです); distinguishing humble in-group family terms (父, 母) from polite out-group family terms (お父さん, お母さん); and learning home-visiting etiquette phrases (ごめんください, お上がりください, いかがですか, いただきます, ごちそうさまでした).

grammar.pattern: Noun (Tool / Means) で Verb [Tools, Instruments, and Methods]
grammar.explanation: In Lesson 5, you learned で for means of transportation (電車で行きます). In Lesson 6, you learned で for location of dynamic action (図書館で勉強します). Here in Lesson 7, で takes on its third major role: marking the TOOL, INSTRUMENT, or MEANS used to perform an action. Formula: 『Noun (Tool/Instrument) + で + Verb』. Typical tools include eating utensils (はしで食べます, スプーンで食べます), cutting tools (はさみで切ります, ナイフで切ります), communication/writing media (パソコンでレポートを書きます), and even physical body parts (手で食べます - eat with hands). Takashi Sensei reminds students: To ask what tool someone uses, say: 『何で [Verb] ますか』 (なん で... — What do you do it with?).

grammar.pattern: Language で Verb & 「Word / Sentence」は ～語で 何ですか [Languages & Translations]
grammar.explanation: Because a spoken or written language is also an instrument or medium of communication, it is marked by the instrument particle で: 『日本語で話します』 (speak in Japanese), 『英語で手紙を書きます』 (write a letter in English). To ask how to say a particular word or phrase in another language, use the set formula: 『「Word / Sentence」は [Language] 語で 何ですか』 (What is '...' in [Language]?). Answer formula: 『「...」です』. Takashi Sensei emphasizes pronouncing 何 as なん before です (なんですか) and remembering to quote the word with quotation brackets 「 」.

grammar.pattern: Person に Noun を あげます [Giving to Others] & The 'Never あげます to Me' Rule
grammar.explanation: The verb あげます means 'to give'. The receiver of the gift is marked by the target particle に: 『[Giver は] Receiver に Object を あげます』. CRITICAL RULE HIGHLIGHTED BY TAKASHI SENSEI: In standard Japanese, あげます can ONLY be used when the giver gives outward to someone else (I give to person B, or Person A gives to Person B). It is a major grammatical violation to use あげます when the receiver is 'ME' (私): ✕「田中さんは私にプレゼントをあげました」 is WRONG! When someone gives something to YOU, you must view the transaction from your perspective using もらいました (私は田中さんにプレゼントをもらいました), or use the special verb くれます (taught in Lesson 24). Never use あげます when the recipient is 私 (watashi)!

examples.translation: I gave flowers to my mother.

grammar.pattern: Person に / から Noun を もらいます [Receiving] & Person に vs. Organization から
grammar.explanation: The verb もらいます means 'to receive'. The giver (the person from whom you receive) is marked by either に or から: 『Receiver は Giver に / から Object を もらいます』. Both に and から are natural when the giver is an individual person: 「先生に本をもらいました」 = 「先生から本をもらいました」. CRITICAL DISTINCTION TAUGHT BY TAKASHI: When receiving an item, money, or parcel from a company, bank, school, or organization (not an individual human being), you CANNOT use に; you MUST use から! Example: 〇「銀行からお金を借りました」 / ✕「銀行に借りました」; 〇「会社からボーナスをもらいました」 / ✕「会社にもらいました」.

grammar.pattern: 貸します (Lend to Person に) vs. 借ります (Borrow from Person に / から)
grammar.explanation:
Keep the directional vectors straight:
• 貸します (かします): Direction flows OUTWARD from subject to recipient ('to lend'). Recipient is marked by に: 『Person A は Person B に [Item] を 貸します』 (A lends [Item] to B).
• 借ります (かります): Direction flows INWARD from source to subject ('to borrow'). Source is marked by に or から: 『Person A は Person B に / から [Item] を 借ります』 (A borrows [Item] from B).
Takashi's memory hook: 貸します (kashimasu) = Cash-out (lending to someone); 借ります (karimasu) = Car-in (borrowing a car into your garage). Organizations must take から: 銀行からお金を借りました.

examples.kanji: 山田さんに傘を貸しました。
examples.kana: やまださんに かさを かしました。
examples.translation: I lent an umbrella to Mr. Yamada.

grammar.pattern: 教えます (Teach to Person に) vs. 習います (Learn from Person に / から)
grammar.explanation:
Another directional pair governed by the same directional logic:
• 教えます (おしえます): Knowledge flows OUTWARD from teacher to student ('to teach'). The learner/recipient takes に: 『Teacher は Student に [Subject] を 教えます』.
• 習います (ならいます): Knowledge flows INWARD from instructor to learner ('to learn'). The instructor takes に or から: 『Student は Teacher に / から [Subject] を 習います』.
If you learn from an institution (e.g. school or university), use から: 学校から習いました.

grammar.pattern: 送ります (Send to) & かけます [電話を~] (Phone Call to Person に / Place へ)
grammar.explanation:
When sending physical items or making calls:
• 送ります (おくります - to send): The recipient person takes に (友達に手紙を送ります), but a destination country or city takes へ or に (アメリカへ荷物を送ります).
• 電話をかけます (でんわをかけます - to make a phone call): The person you call takes に (母に電話をかけます); an office or building you call can take へ or に (会社へ電話をかけます).

grammar.pattern: もう Verb-ました vs. いいえ、まだです [Already Completed vs. Not Yet]
grammar.explanation:
もう means 'already' and indicates that an action is completed at the present moment. It pairs with the past affirmative: 『もう [Verb] ました』. Question: 『もう [Verb] ましたか』 (Have you already done...?).
• Affirmative answer: 『はい、もう [Verb] ました』 (Yes, I have already done so).
• Negative answer: 『いいえ、まだです』 (No, not yet).
TAKASHI SENSEI'S VITAL WARNING: Never answer a 『もう～ましたか』 question with ✕『いいえ、～ませんでした』! Saying 「食べませんでした」 means 'I did not eat (and the opportunity/meal is over; I do not intend to eat)'. Saying 「まだです」 means 'Not yet (I have not eaten yet, but I intend to do so soon)'. Always pair with これから (from now on): 「いいえ、まだです。これから食べます」.

examples.kanji: もう昼ご飯を食べましたか。— はい、もう食べました。
examples.kana: もう ひるごはんを たべましたか。— はい、もう たべました。
examples.translation: Have you already eaten lunch? — Yes, I have already eaten.

examples.kana: もう にもつを おくりましたか。— いいえ、まだです。これから おくります。
examples.translation: Have you sent the parcel already? — No, not yet. I will send it now.

examples.translation: Did you already buy the bullet train tickets? — Yes, I bought them yesterday.

grammar.pattern: Family Terms: Humble In-Group (父・母) vs. Polite Out-Group (お父さん・お母さん)
grammar.explanation:
Japanese etiquette requires strict distinction between your own in-group (内 - uchi) and an outside person's out-group (外 - soto):
• When speaking to an outsider (coworker, client, teacher) about YOUR OWN parents, use the humble terms: 父 (ちち - my father) and 母 (はは - my mother). Never attach さん or お to your own family when speaking to outsiders!
• When referring to SOMEONE ELSE'S parents, or when directly addressing your own parents at home, use the polite honorific terms: お父さん (おとうさん - your/someone's father; Dad!) and お母さん (おかあさん - your/someone's mother; Mom!).
Takashi's rule of thumb: Humble yourself and your family to elevate the listener.

examples.kanji: 私の父は銀行員です。
examples.kana: わたしの ちちは ぎんこういんです。
examples.translation: My father is a bank employee. (Speaking to outsider → 父)

examples.kana: ミラーさんの おとうさんは アメリカに いらっしゃいますか。

grammar.pattern: Home Visiting Etiquette & Hospitality Expressions [ごめんください, お上がりください, etc.]
grammar.explanation:
Lesson 7 introduces the classic script for visiting a Japanese home:
1. Arriving at the entrance (玄関 - genkan): The guest says 『ごめんください』 (Excuse me, is anyone home?).
2. Greeting the guest: The host opens the door and replies 『いらっしゃい』 (Welcome!).
3. Inviting inside: The host invites the guest onto the raised tatami/wooden floor with 『どうぞ お上がりください』 (Please step up and come in).
4. Stepping inside: The guest steps out of their shoes, faces them toward the door, and says 『失礼します』 (しつれいします - Pardon the intrusion).
5. Offering refreshment: The host serves tea or snacks: 『[お茶/コーヒーは] いかがですか』 (How about some tea/coffee?).
6. Partaking: The guest accepts politely: 『いただきます』 (I humbly receive).
7. Complimenting a gift or decoration: 『素敵ですね』 (すてきですね - How lovely!).
8. Finishing: After consuming, the guest thanks the host: 『ごちそうさまでした』 (Thank you for the wonderful treat).

reading.translation: Mr. Miller visits Mr. Yamada's house and calls out 'Gomen kudasai' at the entrance. Yamada's wife warmly welcomes him with 'Irasshai. Douzo oagari kudasai.' Miller says 'Shitsurei shimasu' as he steps inside and gives her flowers from his garden. She thanks him for the lovely gift. Mr. Yamada greets Miller and offers him some coffee ('Koohii wa ikaga desu ka?'). Miller gratefully accepts ('Itadakimasu'). Yamada's wife hands him a spoon, which Miller compliments ('Suteki na supuun desu ne'). Yamada explains that he received it from a colleague in Thailand during last month's business trip. Miller then asks if Yamada has already purchased the bullet train tickets. Yamada replies that he hasn't yet ('Iie, mada desu'), but will buy them online with his smartphone now. Finally, Miller enjoys the cake with a small fork and expresses gratitude after eating with 'Gochisousama deshita'.

questions.question: What phrase does Miller use when announcing his arrival at Yamada's house door?
questions.explanation: When visiting someone's home and arriving at the entrance, a guest calls out 『ごめんください』.

questions.question: How does Yamada's wife invite Miller to step up and enter the house?
options: どうぞお上がりください
questions.explanation: The traditional host phrase to invite someone up into the home is 『どうぞお上がりください』.

questions.question: What present did Miller give to Yamada's wife?
questions.explanation: Miller says: これ、庭の花です。どうぞ (Here are flowers from my garden; please take them).

questions.question: Where did Mr. Yamada get the lovely spoon from?
options: He received it from a coworker in Thailand
He bought it at a department store in Osaka
He borrowed it from Mr. Miller
His father gave it to him for Christmas
questions.explanation: Yamada states: タイへ行きました。会社の人にもらいました (I went to Thailand; I received it from someone at the company).

questions.question: Has Mr. Yamada already bought the bullet train ticket?
options: No, not yet; he will buy it now on his smartphone
Yes, he bought it at the station yesterday
No, he will never buy it
Yes, Miller bought it for him
questions.explanation: Yamada answers: いいえ、まだです。これからネットで買います (No, not yet. I will buy it online now).

questions.question: Which tool does Miller use to eat the cake?
options: A small fork (小さなフォーク)
questions.explanation: Yamada offers: 小さなフォークで食べます (Eat it with a small fork).

questions.question: What phrase does Miller say before drinking the coffee?
questions.explanation: Before partaking in food or drink offered to you, say 『いただきます』.

questions.question: Why does Yamada say 『会社の人にもらいました』 instead of 『あげました』?
options: Because Yamada is the recipient receiving the spoon into his possession
Because Yamada gave the spoon away to his company
Because あげます cannot be used for spoons
Because もらいました means to lend
questions.explanation: もらいました means 'received from'; Yamada received the spoon from his coworker.

exercises.question: When asking a friend about THEIR mother, which word must you use?
exercises.explanation: To refer politely to someone else's mother, use お母さん (おかあさん).

exercises.question: What does a guest say when entering someone's house at the door?
exercises.explanation: A visiting guest announces arrival at the entrance with 『ごめんください』.

exercises.question: What does the host say to invite the guest onto the raised floor of the home?
options: どうぞお上がりください
exercises.explanation: Hosts invite visitors inside using 『どうぞお上がりください』.

exercises.question: What does the guest say when stepping into someone's home?
options: 失礼します (しつれいします)

exercises.explanation: Polite offer: 『[Noun] は いかがですか』 (How about [Noun]?).

exercises.question: What should you say immediately before partaking in a meal or beverage?
exercises.explanation: Say 『いただきます』 (literally 'I humbly receive') before eating or drinking.

exercises.question: What should you say after finishing a meal offered by a host?
exercises.explanation: Say 『ごちそうさまでした』 after finishing food or drink to thank the provider.

writing.title: Giving and Receiving Gifts, Daily Tools, and Learning Japanese
writing.prompt: Write 6–8 sentences in Japanese applying Lesson 7 grammar. (1) Describe what tools or utensils you use to eat, write, or work (use で). (2) Explain how to say one of your favorite words in Japanese using 『「...」は日本語で「...」です』. (3) Describe a gift you gave to a family member or friend using 『[Person] に [Gift] を あげました』. (4) Describe a gift you received from someone or borrowed from an institution using 『[Person] に/から もらいました』 or 『[Place] から 借りました』. (5) State an action you have already finished (もう～ました) and an action you have not yet finished (まだです).
writing.placeholder:
私はいつも ______ でご飯を食べます。パソコンで ______ を書きます。
「______」は日本語で「______」です。
誕生日に ______ に ______ をあげました。
そして、______ に ______ をもらいました。
もう ______ を ______ ました。でも、______ はまだです。これから ______ ます。
writing.modelAnswer: 私はいつもはしでご飯を食べます。そして、スマホで写真を撮ります。「Thank you」は日本語で「ありがとう」です。先月、母の誕生日にきれいな花をあげました。そして、クリスマスに父に新しい時計をもらいました。今週の宿題はもうしました。でも、部屋の掃除はまだです。これから掃除をします。

dialogues.speaker: 同僚
dialogues.prompt: もう昼ご飯を食べましたか。

options.text: いいえ、まだです。これから食べます。
いいえ、食べませんでした。

dialogues.tip: Answer 'not yet' with いいえ、まだです (never 食べませんでした).

dialogues.situation: Asking where a gift came from
dialogues.speaker: 友達
dialogues.prompt: 素敵なネクタイですね。誰にもらいましたか。

options.text: 誕生日に父にもらいました。

dialogues.tip: To say you received it from your father: 父にもらいました.

dialogues.speaker: 留学生
dialogues.tip: Answer a translation question simply with: 『「Word」です』.

dialogues.speaker: 同僚
dialogues.prompt: すみません、そのはさみをちょっと貸してください。
dialogues.tip: Respond to a request to lend with: はい、どうぞ (Yes, here you go).

dialogues.speaker: 友達
dialogues.prompt: クリスマスに友達に何をあげますか。

options.text: マフラーをもらいますか。

dialogues.tip: You give outward to a friend: [Item] を あげます.

dialogues.speaker: 訪問者
dialogues.prompt: とてもおいしかったです。
dialogues.tip: Express gratitude after eating with ごちそうさまでした.

dialogues.speaker: 友達
dialogues.prompt: 誰に日本語を習いましたか。

options.text: タカシ先生に習いました。
タカシ先生に教えました。
タカシ先生から教えました。

dialogues.tip: I learned from Teacher Takashi: タカシ先生に習いました.

dialogues.speaker: 母
dialogues.prompt: もう荷物を送りましたか。

options.text: はい、もう送りましたよ。
いいえ、もう送りました。

dialogues.tip: Confirming completion: はい、もう [Verb] ました.

dialogues.situation: Talking about an outside person's parent
dialogues.speaker: 同僚
dialogues.prompt: 佐藤さんの___はお元気ですか。
dialogues.tip: Use お父さん (polite) when speaking of someone else's father.
